data.narrative:
XMOS is a Growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised £200M+ to date. The relevant comp universe spans 12 private companies in Chips & Semiconductors (including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems) alongside 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Only one valuation method was applicable to XMOS given available data constraints. Stage-progression anchoring uses the £200M+ total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement, implying a valuation of £240M. Peer-median benchmarking could not be applied: while 12 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three met narrow filters on stage, adjacent-stage status, or valuation tier, which would make a median comparison unreliable. Public-comp anchoring was also inapplicable because XMOS's revenue is not disclosed—a standard constraint for private companies—and applying the 21.5x median P/S multiple from public semiconductor comps would be speculative.

The analysis supports a valuation range of £204M to £276M, centered on £240M, though this estimate relies on a single methodological anchor. The primary uncertainty is the absence of meaningful peer transaction or valuation data at XMOS's stage and within its specific subsector focus. A fuller triangulation would require either disclosed revenue, access to private benchmark multiples, or comparable M&A precedents in frontier semiconductor infrastructure.
